frames.why: 可以 = can, may. What you're asking for goes in the middle; 嗎 at the end makes it a question. The polite way to ask for anything.
給 = give. 給我 + the thing = give me the thing. Wrap it to be polite: 可以給我 … 嗎？ or 請給我 …
用 = use. The tool or language comes before the action: 用英文解釋 = use English, explain (explain in English). 用中文說 = say it in Chinese.
怎麼 = how. 怎麼 + verb = how to do it: 怎麼說 = how (to) say. The thing you're asking about comes first.
Say it as a statement and add 嗎: 你是學生 (you are a student) → 你是學生嗎？ (are you a student?). Nothing else moves.

frames.zh: question word where the answer goes
frames.why: Chinese doesn't move the question word to the front. 你喜歡喝什麼？ = you like drink what? The answer takes its place: 我喜歡喝咖啡.
Say the verb, 不 (or 沒 for 有), then the verb again: 要不要 = want not want? It asks yes or no without 嗎. Answer with the verb: 要 / 不要.
Where comes before what you do: 我在中文大學工作 = I at CUHK work. English puts the place last; Chinese puts it first.
在 right before a verb = in the middle of doing it: 我在學中文 = I'm learning Chinese.
不 sits right before the verb or adjective it cancels: 我不知道 = I not know. 不太 + adjective = not very.
想 + verb = would like to (soft). 要 + thing = want, I'll have (direct, normal when ordering). The thing or action follows right after.
Chinese says what you like doing with the verb in: 我喜歡喝咖啡 = I like drink coffee. Leave out 喝 and it sounds like you like coffee as a thing.

frames.en: (do it) a bit, for a moment
frames.why: 一下 after a verb makes it small and soft: 等一下 = wait a moment, 解釋一下 = explain a little. It makes a request sound friendly.
A number can't go straight before a noun: it needs a measure word. 一杯咖啡 = one cup coffee. 個 is the all-purpose one: 一個人.
請 at the front makes any request polite: 請說慢一點 = please speak a bit slower. Nothing else in the sentence changes.
還 = still. 還好 = still good (okay), 還可以 = still acceptable (not bad), 還沒 = still not (not yet), 還不太會 = still can't really.

Chinese starts with where and when: 在香港，大家用哪些大模型？ = in Hong Kong, everyone uses which large models? English puts the place last. Then who, then the verb, then the thing; a question word (哪些 which ones, 哪個 which) simply takes the thing's place.
